public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 218

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/218](https://www.erdosproblems.com/218)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos218

/--
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is followed by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_218.variants.le : {n | primeGap n ≤ primeGap (n + 1)}.HasDensity <| 1 / 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is preceded by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_218.variants.ge : {n | primeGap (n + 1) ≤ primeGap n}.HasDensity <| 1 / 2 := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many indices $n$ such that the prime gap at $n$ is equal to the prime gap
at $n+1$. This is equivalent to the existence of infinitely many arithmetic progressions of
length $3$, see `erdos_141.variants.infinite_three`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_218.variants.infinite_equal_prime_gap : {n | primeGap n = primeGap (n + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos218

findings.description: The docstring's second sentence claims equivalence with the existence of infinitely many arithmetic progressions of length 3, omitting “of consecutive primes.” Unrestricted length-three arithmetic progressions trivially exist infinitely often. The Lean statement correctly requires equal gaps between three consecutive primes; only the explanatory sentence is inaccurate.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/218, read through its 9 July 2026 archived page, states “there are infinitely many n such that d_{n+1}=d_n.” Its remarks explicitly describe the associated progressions as “consecutive primes in arithmetic progression” and link Problem 141. Wikipedia's “Consecutive primes in arithmetic progression” section likewise distinguishes this condition from ordinary prime arithmetic progressions.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the second sentence to “This is equivalent to the existence of infinitely many arithmetic progressions of three consecutive primes.” Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

sources_consulted: Local Mathlib: Mathlib/Data/Nat/Nth.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Prime/Nth.lean; Mathlib/NumberTheory/PrimeCounting.lean; Mathlib/Data/Set/Card.lean
review.notes: All three Lean statements faithfully match the source, including both non-strict inequalities. The sole finding is a minor documentation omission. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully: they verify initial gap values, positivity of every gap, the equal-gap/midpoint equivalence, and the standard real-valued natural-density formula. Zero-based indexing and the density ratio's value at N = 0 do not change the claims. Direct requests to erdosproblems.com encountered a browser challenge; the archived source and the separately maintained current problem database both record the problem as open.
